The writ Court on 05.05.2016 while disposing of Writ-C No. 45331 of 2009 passed the following order:-
"1. Heard Sri R.S. Umrao, learned counsel for petitioners and learned Standing Counsel as well as Sri P.K. Singh, Advocate for respondents.
2. Petitioners claim to own disputed plot measuring 1426.56 sq. meters in Gata No.
251, Village Mau, District Moradabad which they claim to have purchased vide sale deed dated 31.01.1998.

sentences.text: It is admitted by Sri P.K. Singh, learned counsel appearing for Moradabad Development Authority (hereinafter referred to as the "MDA") that alleged land of petitioners has not been acquired by Development Authority after following procedure prescribed under Land Acquisition Act, 1894 though occupied and in possession of MDA.

However, it is stated that if petitioners agree, they may be paid compensation determining market value as per the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 2013").
4.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: To this offer learned counsel appearing for petitioners expresses, his willingness and stated that petitioners are ready to give up their rights and shall execute appropriate documents transferring title in case compensation as per Act, 2013 is paid to them within three months.

5. In view of above and with the consent of parties, this writ petition is disposed of directing MDA (respondent no. 2) to compute compensation of disputed land in accordance with the provisions of Act, 2013 and pay the same to petitioners within a period of three months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order and petitioners thereupon and simultaneously shall execute documents in respect of land in question which may have the effect of transferring title of disputed land to respondent no. 2."
Pursuant to order of writ Court, a compliance affidavit has been filed by opposite party on 01.01.2023 wherein in para no. 6, it has been stated that the computation of the land has been done and amount of compensation to be paid to applicant is Rs.50,21,491.20/-.
In para no. 7, it has been stated that cheque was drawn in the name of the all the three applicants but they refused to accept the said amount.
Learned counsel appearing for Development Authority states that they are seeking enhancement of the compensation so awarded.

This Court after perusing the material on record finds that matter regarding quantum of compensation and its enhancement cannot be gone into by contempt Court exercising power under Section 12 of Contempt of Courts Act.

Moreover, the writ Court had only directed to compute the compensation of the land to be paid to the applicants and as the amount has already been computed and authorities have tried to hand over the cheque to the applicant which the applicants have refused, no case for contempt is made out.
The contempt application is misconceived and stands dismissed.
